primary_work.title: On the Identifiability of Causal Abstractions
primary_work.code_status: no paper-specific immutable official repository with pinned dependencies and reproduction commands verified from the inspected primary records

decision: NARROWED BEYOND INTERVENTION-INDUCED CAUSAL ABSTRACTION IDENTIFIABILITY — NOT ADOPTED
rejected_claims: non-atomic unknown interventions require language before any causal structure can be recovered
failure to recover individual latent variables means no causal representation is identifiable
discovering intervention-induced latent blocks is itself a new language-grounding principle
naming quotient blocks with natural language refines the causal abstraction
task success or language-shuffle gaps prove recovery inside an abstraction block
an arbitrary fine-grained target partition is valid ground truth when the intervention family identifies only a coarser quotient
remaining_rq: After computing the maximal causal abstraction identifiable from the unknown intervention family and complete non-language paired trajectory, can a preregistered externally fixed language law distinguish members inside a residual quotient block, jointly identify raw-utterance equivalence and the finer intervention-target partition, and eliminate every within-block joint automorphism?
